verdict.rationale: Calendly ships an official MCP server that agents can use as a tool. Its documentation lists the tools exposed, including creating event types, and turns natural-language booking commands into Calendly API calls. Calendly also documents an AI-agent scheduling pattern for end-to-end booking and API endpoints that return availability for specific event types. missing for 10: explicit evidence that availability lookup and listing existing bookings are exposed as named MCP tools (the cited availability evidence is REST-only), and independent or hands-on corroboration of the MCP server in agent use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, agents can use my scheduling account as a tool — an MCP server or tool-calling surface exposes availability, bookings, and event types

citations.quote: Bring scheduling actions into your AI apps through natural conversation, powered by Calendly MCP.
Below is the complete list of tools exposed by the Calendly MCP server, organized by category with the equivalent REST endpoint for each.
event\_types-create\_event\_type | Create a new event type
It translates natural-language commands (e.g., "Book a 30-minute meeting with Sam next Tuesday") into structured Calendly API calls with no need to implement raw REST requests.
Enable AI assistants or agents in your product to **book meetings end‑to‑end** via Calendly's Scheduling API endpoint.
Calendly users can retrieve information about availability for a specific event type
